hypotheses.justification: Nothing in the statement or proof needs this instance. `coe_τ` takes it only because `M` appears in the statement and Lean auto-includes instance-implicit section variables in theorems. `modularFunctionFieldBar` is declared under `variable (N : ℕ)` with no NeZero (Def_ModularCurve_ArithmeticGalois.lean, lines 109–113). Its body is `laurentBaseChange (AlgebraicClosure ℚ) (modularFunctionFieldFull N)`, and `modularFunctionFieldFull N := IntermediateField.adjoin ℚ (divisorExpansions N)` (Def_ModularCurve_X0.lean, line 305). `divisorExpansions` only uses `NeZero d` for the divisors `d`, never `NeZero N`; that `modularFunctionFieldBar` elaborates without the instance confirms neither definition takes it. `τ` is a definition whose body `arithmeticRingAut (modularFunctionFieldFull M) σ` never uses `NeZero M`, and Lean drops unused section variables from definitions, so `τ` takes only `M` and `σ`. `laurentBaseChange` and `arithmeticRingAut` are generic in the intermediate field. So with `omit [NeZero M] in` the statement still elaborates and the proof is still `rfl`: `τ M σ x` unfolds definitionally to the subtype element whose value is `coeffMap (σ : Lb →+* Lb) (x : LaurentSeries Lb)`. There is no degenerate case: for `M = 0` the field is still a well-defined intermediate field and the identity holds by definition.
